Tune Candidate Workflows to Impute One Numeric Variable

Source: R/tune_impute_workflows.R
tune_impute_workflows.Rd

Benchmarks every combination of candidate recipes and models for predicting one numeric variable from the others, by cross-validated RMSE, and uses the best one to fill in the variable's missing values. It wraps the `workflowsets::workflow_set()` plus `finetune::tune_race_anova()` scaffold that was repeated for each imputed variable.

Usage

tune_impute_workflows(
  data,
  target,
  recipes = NULL,
  models = NULL,
  folds = 5,
  grid = 10,
  race = TRUE,
  seed = 123,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

target

Name of the numeric column to impute.

recipes

Named list of `recipes::recipe()` objects with `target` as the outcome, or `NULL` for one default recipe (all other columns as predictors; median / mode imputation of the predictors, dummy variables, zero-variance filter).

models

Named list of `parsnip` regression model specifications, or `NULL` for a linear model (`parsnip::linear_reg()`).

folds

Number of cross-validation folds (default 5), or an `rsample` resampling object built on the rows of `data` where `target` is observed.

grid

Number of tuning candidates per workflow (default 10), or a grid data frame.

race

If `TRUE` (default), tune with `finetune::tune_race_anova()` (needs at least three folds); otherwise with `tune::tune_grid()`. Workflows without tuning parameters are simply resampled.

seed

Random seed (default 123).

verbose

Passed to `workflowsets::workflow_map()`.

Value

A list of class `cbe_impute_tune` with

ranking

one row per workflow (its best candidate): `wflow_id`, `rmse`, `std_err`, `n`, `rank`, ordered best first

metrics

RMSE of every candidate of every workflow

best_workflow_id, best_params

the winner and its tuning parameter values

predictions

out-of-fold predictions of the winner: `Fold`, `.row` (row of `data`), `observed` and `imputed`, ready for [plot_imputed_vs_observed()]

rmse, null_rmse, rse

see Null model and RSE

fit

the winner fitted to all rows with an observed `target`

data

`data` with the missing values of `target` filled in

n_imputed, target

number of filled values, and the target name

What is tuned on

Only rows where `target` is observed are used for resampling and for the final fit; rows where it is missing are predicted at the end. Predictors may have missing values only if the recipe deals with them (the default recipe imputes them with the median or mode).

Null model and RSE

`null_rmse` is the cross-validated RMSE of predicting every held-out value with the mean of `target` in the corresponding training folds, and `rse = (rmse / null_rmse)^2` for the best workflow, both from the same folds. An RSE below 1 beats the mean. This is the training-mean baseline of [tune_impute_numeric()], not the oracle baseline of [compare_imputation_rse()].

Cost and reproducibility

Every workflow is tuned over `grid` candidates on every fold, so the run time grows with `length(recipes) * length(models) * grid * folds`. Racing drops poor candidates after the first three folds. Results depend on `seed` (folds, grids and models that use random numbers).

See also

[plot_tune_grid_rmse()], [tbl_tune_best_model()], [plot_imputed_vs_observed()], [tune_impute_numeric()], [compare_imputation_rse()]

Examples

# \donttest{
ok <- vapply(c("workflowsets", "finetune", "tune", "rsample", "parsnip", "workflows", "yardstick"),
             requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
if (all(ok)) {
  d <- mtcars
  d$mpg[c(3, 11, 20)] <- NA
  res <- tune_impute_workflows(d, "mpg", folds = 3, race = FALSE)
  tbl_tune_best_model(res)
}
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>    rank workflow  rmse std_err n_folds null_rmse   rse selected
#>   <int> <chr>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <int>     <dbl> <dbl> <lgl>   
#> 1     1 base_lm   3.81   0.219       3      5.79 0.433 TRUE    
# }
